'''Kalobaran Maiti''' (born 21 October 1967) is an Indian [[physicist]] specialising in [[condensed matter physics]] and [[materials science]]. He obtained his MSc degree from [[Rajabazar Science College]] and PhD degree from [[Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore]]. He was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] in 2010, the highest science award in India, in the [[physical science]]s category<ref>{{cite web|title=Shanti Swarup Bhatngar Awards 2010|url=http://www.dst.gov.in/awards/award10.htm|publisher=Department of Science & Technology, Govt. of India|access-date=4 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140702115742/http://dst.gov.in/awards/award10.htm|archive-date=2 July 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> for his contribution in the field of very high resolution photoelectron spectroscopy in understanding the physics of metal-insulator transition, charge density wave and Kondo systems.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brief Profile of the Awardee|url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=136|publisher=CSIR Human Resource Development Group|access-date=4 November 2015}}</ref>  He is also  a 
Fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nasi.org.in/fellows/maiti-kalobaran/|title=FASTPANEL|website=Nasi.org.in|access-date=7 November 2026}}</ref>{{citation needed|date=November 2018}} [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fellows.ias.ac.in/profile/v/FL2010029|title=Indian Academy of Sciences|website=Fellows.ias.ac.in|access-date=7 November 2026}}</ref> and the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.insa.nic.in/writereaddata/UpLoadedFiles/PINSA/Vol81_2015_5_Art14.pdf | title=Academy News - Annual General Meeting | pages=1246–1247 | work=Proceedings of the Indian National Science Academy | date=5 December 2015 | volume=81 | issue=5 | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | access-date=27 November 2018 }}</ref>

He is a Professor of [[Condensed matter physics|Condensed Matter Physics]] and [[Materials science|Materials Science]] at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], Mumbai (TIFR). At TIFR, Maiti has built an electron spectrometer that can measure the energy of electrons with very high accuracy.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dinesh C. Sharma|title=Indian scientists explore fresh research frontiers|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/indian-scientists-explore-fresh-research-frontiers-84249-2010-10-20|access-date=4 November 2015|publisher=India Today|date=21 October 2010}}</ref> He was appointed as the Director of the [[Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science]], Kolkata on 19 March 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title= Director - Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science |url=https://www.iacs.res.in/maincontroller.php?navid=17&subnavid=48|website=Iacs.res.in}}</ref>
